findings.lens: Anabaptist / Mennonite (Schleitheim Confession, Confession of Faith in a Mennonite Perspective 1995)
findings.claim: Matthew 18:20 is missing; it is the Anabaptist worship and ecclesiology text.
findings.evidence: 'Where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I among them' is the ground of the free-church claim that the gathered congregation, not a rite or a building, is where Christ is present; it sits behind statement 4 as well.
findings.fix: Add 'Matthew 18:20' to the Worship key passages.

findings.claim: Missing the texts liturgical Christians cite for the word-and-sacrament shape of worship and the heavenly liturgy.
findings.evidence: Luke 24:28-35 (CCC 1347 reads the Emmaus meal as the shape of the Mass); Revelation 4-5 (CCC 1136-1139); Acts 20:7.

findings.claim: Statement 18 asks about weekly communion but Acts 20:7, the one text everyone cites for it, is not among the passages; Ephesians 5:19, the companion of Colossians 3:16 and the a cappella text, is also absent.
findings.evidence: Acts 20:7 'upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread'; Eph 5:19 'singing and making melody in your heart'. Both appear in every Restoration statement on worship.

findings.claim: The texts the liturgical side actually reaches for, the heavenly liturgy, are absent; the list is weighted to the free side's proof texts (John 4, 1 Cor 14, Psalm 150).
findings.evidence: Isaiah 6:1-3 and Revelation 4-5 supply the Trisagion and the Sanctus; Hebrews 8:1-5 grounds earthly worship in the heavenly sanctuary.

findings.lens: Presbyterian / Reformed (Westminster Standards, Three Forms of Unity)
findings.claim: None of the regulative-principle texts appear, so the passage list presents the axis as liturgy versus spontaneity only.
findings.evidence: WCF 21.1 prooftexts: Deuteronomy 12:32, Exodus 20:4-6, Matthew 15:9; Leviticus 10:1-3 (Nadab and Abihu) is the sermon text every Reformed hearer knows on this subject.

findings.claim: Statement 18 asserts weekly communion, but the only New Testament text for weekly frequency, Acts 20:7 ('on the first day of the week, when we were gathered together to break bread'), is not listed. The free pole has no Spirit-led text beyond John 4:23-24; Ephesians 5:18-20 ('be filled with the Spirit... singing and making melody... with your heart') is what free-worship writers actually cite. Matthew 6:7-13 is a natural read-both-ways addition: v.7 against 'empty phrases' for the free pole, v.9 'Pray then like this' as the Lord's own set form for the liturgical pole.
findings.evidence: Calvin, Institutes IV.17.43-46, argues weekly communion from Acts 2:42 and 20:7; the Restoration Movement built its weekly Supper on Acts 20:7. Frame, Worship in Spirit and Truth (in read_more), ch. 1-2, works from John 4:24 and Ephesians 5:18-20; Anglican and Orthodox apologists for set prayer cite Matthew 6:9 and Luke 11:2 ('When you pray, say...').
